# Independent audit of stochastic section centroids, and two exact supplements

Sources read in full:

* `candidate 6a014eb26413a72b`;
* `candidate 8095e181b6be7bf1`;
* `candidate f5d111431879f6ef`.



## 1. Audit of the necessary conditions

For a row `(epsilon,b_1,...,b_d)` with all b_j>0, the cap-ratio formula below the smallest positive knot y is exact and strictly decreasing in its threshold. A minimizing threshold therefore lies in [y,max b]. At epsilon=0 the ratio equals GM(b) through y and is strictly larger afterward. Compactness and continuity of these positive-threshold cap distributions force every chosen minimizing threshold to tend to y. The full-orthant lower estimate and the value at y then squeeze the one-sided derivative to

    GM(b)[1/y−(Σ_j 1/b_j)/d].

The expansion is uniform for thresholds converging to y>0. Repeated positive knots do not affect the argument. When all b_j=y the capacity is exactly y, giving derivative zero, including d=1.

A nonzero row with r zeros, 2≤r≤d, can have r−1 zero entries raised while one remains zero. Its gain is exactly a positive constant times epsilon^((r−1)/d), while the full funding row loses only O(epsilon). The latter follows from monotonicity and homogeneity by coordinatewise multiplicative bounds; it needs no full-row differentiability. Thus this row status is excluded at a maximum. The all-zero row correctly remains separate.

For a full proper regular row at a differentiable capacity point, the fixed-minimizer ratio is an upper support touching the capacity. Opposite perturbations identify their gradients. The coarea identity and tF'=dF give

    ∂_j phi=F^(−1/d)b_j,

where b is the actual section centroid. Properness makes every b_j positive. Two full regular rows therefore have the same normalized weighted gradient, as stated.

Column-preserving transfers between the full row and a positive entry of a one-zero row are feasible in both signs. They give x_ij=mu_i/lambda_j and c_i=d GM(lambda_except_h), with mu_i=c_i g_i/d. Applying the preceding one-sided zero derivative gives exactly

    d max_{j≠h}lambda_j≤Σ_j lambda_j.

Two distinct holes imply lambda_j≤(Σlambda)/d for every column. The all-zero-row inequality must instead be obtained by adding an arbitrary row with a selected zero coordinate; minimizing the corresponding weighted linear cost per geometric mean gives the stated constraint for every hole. This is necessary only and is not substituted for all possible full-row directions.

Rows with the same hole have equal c_i and proportional positive entries, so merging preserves the objective exactly, not merely monotonically. Distinct surviving holes give an injective partial matching and can be placed on the diagonal by a column permutation. The full row and any all-zero rows occupy unmatched labels. Neither their weights nor their missing-entry restrictions are dropped.

With exactly one full row, Euler homogeneity and the column equations give H=S, mu=S(1−t)/d, and

    (1−x_j)b_j/(1−t)=1/d−mu_j/[S(1−t)]≤1/d.

Equality holds precisely at the unmatched labels, including the full-row label. The normalized diagonal image of the actual section has exactly this centroid. Collapsed coordinates are correctly allowed and no unjustified inverse map is used.

## 2. Actual-facet divergence identities

Let Δ be the standard barycentric d-simplex, let x be strictly positive, and let t be a proper regular stationary threshold for t/F_x(t)^(1/d). Let

    C={ξ∈Δ:x·ξ≤t},       F=|C|/|Δ|,
    S={ξ∈Δ:x·ξ=t},       b=centroid(S).

For every j let Δ_j={ξ_j=0} be the opposite facet and let F_j be the relative (d−1)-volume fraction of C∩Δ_j in Δ_j. Denote the centroid of C by c and that of C∩Δ_j by c^(j). Then

    F_j=(x_j/t)F>0,                                      (10)
    (d+1)c_l=1+d(1−x_l/t)b_l,                            (11)
    c_l^(j)=[t+d(x_j−x_l)b_l]/(d x_j),  l≠j.             (12)

In particular all coordinates on the right of (12) are strictly positive. Hence

    d(x_l−x_j)b_l<t  whenever x_l>x_j.                   (13)

These are actual facet-incidence constraints, not a scalar Schur-product estimate.

Proof. Work in the affine hyperplane Σξ_j=1 with its Euclidean volume. The tangent affine vector field V_j(ξ)=e_j−ξ has divergence −d. On each old facet other than j its outward normal flux is zero; on facet j the flux equals minus the altitude h_j of e_j above that facet. On the cutting face it equals (x_j−t)/||grad_Δ x||. Since h_j|Δ_j|=d|Δ| and F'=|S|/(||grad_Δ x|| |Δ|), divergence gives

    dF_j=dF+(x_j−t)F'.

Stationarity tF'=dF proves (10). In particular every captured facet has positive relative volume; a full-positive regular stationary cap cannot be a one-vertex cap.

Now use ξ_l V_j. Its divergence is δ_jl−(d+1)ξ_l. The same boundary calculation gives

    δ_jl F−(d+1)F c_l
       =−d F_j c_l^(j)+(x_j−t)F' b_l.                    (14)

For j=l the facet coordinate c_j^(j) vanishes. Substituting stationarity in (14) gives (11). For j≠l, substitute (10) and (11) into (14); cancellation gives (12). Since the captured facet has positive relative volume, its centroid has strictly positive barycentric coordinates on that facet. This proves (13). All fluxes are on finitely many flat faces of an actual convex polytope, so the elementary divergence theorem applies without smooth-boundary assumptions. ∎

The captured-facet centroid also satisfies x·c^(j)<t. Using (12) gives another exact necessary inequality:

    d Σ_l x_l² b_l > t Σ_{l≠j}x_l   for every j.         (15)

The strictness follows because a positive-volume captured facet contains points with strict cut inequality. Equations (10)–(15) do not by themselves give a support theorem for a stochastic maximum.

## 3. An exact stationary saddle showing that current multipliers need not be dual feasible

Take d=3 and

    X_1=(1/5,1/5,3/5,3/5),
    X_2=(0,0,0,0),
    X_3=(2/5,2/5,0,2/5),
    X_4=(2/5,2/5,2/5,0),
    c=(2^(−1/3),3/4,3/4,3/4).

The columns sum to one. At the full row, put U=Ξ_3+Ξ_4. Uniform tetrahedral measure gives U the Beta(2,2) density 6u(1−u); the row value is 1/5+(2/5)U. Its unique capacity-minimizing threshold is

    t=2/5,       F=1/2,       b=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4).

Indeed on the proper interval, F=3u²−2u³ and the sign of the ratio derivative is the sign of u(2u−1). The ratio outside the support cannot give a smaller value. The section is the product of the two pair simplices, so its stated centroid is exact.

The multipliers are lambda_j=1/4. All equations and inequalities (4)–(9) of the audited source hold, with mu_1=mu_2=0 and mu_3=mu_4=1/10. In particular

    ((1−x_j)b_j/(1−t))_j=(1/3,1/3,1/6,1/6).

The weighted objective equals one. Nevertheless the full-row weight is not feasible for the current dual multipliers:

    c_1=2^(−1/3)>3/4=3 GM(lambda_except_1),

as follows by cubing and comparing 1/2>27/64. This does not disprove stochastic containment, because support may be paid by a different dual choice or by a better zero-diagonal competitor.

The point is not a local maximum. Perturb the full row by epsilon(1,−1,0,0), and both rows 3 and 4 by epsilon(−1/2,1/2,0,0), keeping row 2 zero. This is a feasible two-sided path for sufficiently small epsilon. Its weighted first derivative is zero, while

    H''(0)=5/6−5/16−5/16=5/24>0.                       (16)

Here are exact derivations retaining the optimized threshold. Conditionally on U=u, the low-coordinate split W=Ξ_1−Ξ_2 has mean zero and second moment (1−u)²/3. Therefore the CDF second derivative at fixed t is

    F_epsilon,epsilon
       =∂_t[ 2u(1−u)³/(2/5) ]=−25/8

at u=1/2. Exchange symmetry gives F_epsilon=F_epsilon,t=0. At the minimizing threshold the ratio has strictly positive second t derivative: the derivative of F−tF'/3 is 5/2 there. The implicit-function theorem and the strict global threshold minimum give a unique nearby minimizing threshold, with first variation zero. Thus threshold optimization does not alter the second epsilon derivative. Multiplication by c_1=F^(1/3) gives the weighted full-row second derivative

    −t F_epsilon,epsilon/(3F)=5/6.

Each other positive row has weighted capacity

    (3/10)(1−25 epsilon²/16)^(1/3),

whose second derivative is −5/16. This proves (16) and a strict objective increase for all sufficiently small nonzero epsilon. The regularity and global-threshold persistence hold because the threshold stays strictly between the two separated knot groups; compactness of the positive-threshold minimization excludes remote switches.

Thus the section-centroid equations supply genuine geometric restrictions, but necessary first-order conditions and current-multiplier feasibility must remain distinct. A second-order support argument is a separate obligation.

## 4. Exact independent checks

`supporting computation verify_stochastic_section_centroid_divergence_audit_two_sided.py` passes 25,402 exact checks. For 686 distinct rational tetrahedral cut geometries whose stationary row shift is fully positive, it independently computes every actual captured facet polygon and its centroid, then verifies (10), (12), (13), and (15). It also verifies the low-dimensional zero-entry derivatives, the stationary matrix equations, and all rational saddle Hessian constants. These finite checks supplement the all-dimensional divergence proofs; they do not establish an unproved higher-dimensional stochastic theorem.
